title: Frozen vegetable VFFS machine, jaw drive seizure
tests: Equipment failure in a food plant (not process); forced deterioration from wash-down; mixed quality of tree.
summary: The sealing jaw drive of a vertical form-fill-seal machine seized after the slide bushes ran dry. High-pressure wash-down removed grease. Tree notes the dry bushes but not why: no wash-down guard, lube task after wash-down missing.

problem.title: Sealing jaw slide seizure on VFFS-04
problem.whatHappened: On 6 Mar 2026 the jaw drive on VFFS-04 faulted on high servo torque and the jaws stopped open. The linear slide bushes were dry and scored and one had seized on the rail. The machine was stripped and the bushes and rail were replaced.
problem.where: Linear slide bushes and rail of the sealing jaw carriage.
problem.when: Start of the shift after the nightly wash-down.
problem.impact: Line down 18 hours until the rail and bushes arrived. Frozen product held in the freezer buffer; partial run scrapped.
problem.makeModel: Vertical form-fill-seal bagger, servo jaw drive
problem.duty: Bags 1 kg frozen mixed vegetables, 55 bags per minute

otherCosts.description: Product warmed above limit and scrapped

evidence.title: Slide bushes and rail
evidence.note: Bushes dry and scored, rail with fretting marks and rust spots. No grease in the housings.

evidence.title: PM plan for VFFS-04
evidence.note: Weekly lube task for the slides scheduled on Sunday. Wash-down runs nightly Monday to Saturday.

evidence.title: Sanitation procedure
evidence.note: High-pressure hot wash with the jaws open. No cover on the slides. No re-lube step after wash-down.

evidence.title: Wash crew lead
evidence.note: Said the jaw area is washed because that is where product builds up; no instruction on avoiding the slides.

mustSuggest.idea: Sanitation and maintenance not planned together: no re-lube step after wash-down
Slides not designed for wash-down: no covers or sealed bearings, or wrong lubricant type
Grease type not water-resistant for a wash-down area
Wash crew has no instruction on which parts to avoid

acceptable: Servo torque trending as a monitor
Sealed or stainless linear bearing upgrade
wrongOrDangerous: The wash crew washed the machine wrongly (blame)

mustFlag.note: No interval, craft or task detail
No condition monitoring or spares action

mustNotFlag: blame (n2 describes the wash practice neutrally)
challenge.expectation: Mostly sound. At most 4 issues, mostly medium or low.
deliberateWeaknesses: a2 and a3 have no interval or craft (no_task_interval on a2 if a task)
n4 hypothesis with no evidence and no link
No spares action (12 days lead time)
No condition monitoring of torque or bush wear
Rollout to other VFFS machines not mentioned

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Grease washed out by nightly wash-down is forcing wear we caused. Remove the cause (cover, grease type, re-lube) rather than shortening the bush interval.

preventive.what: Re-lube jaw slides with a water-resistant grease after each wash-down and before start-up
Stainless splash covers or sealed linear bearings on the jaw slides
Sanitation procedure: avoid direct spray on the slides and re-lube step before start
Servo torque trend and an alarm on rising jaw drive torque
Hold a bush set and rail section for the jaw carriage

capa.spares: A bush set and short rail section; 12 days normal lead time.
capa.rollout: All VFFS machines and other washed-down linear slides in the plant: check lube and covers.
unacceptable: Shorten the bush replacement interval as the countermeasure
Food-safety claims about the lubricant (it must be food grade, the site decides)
